title: LLM Porting Session: OpenAI/Anthropic → Redwood API (porting + parity checks)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Veridian Health through a practical porting runbook: API parity for completions, chat, streaming, embeddings, and function-calling. Discussed token accounting differences, VPC/private deployment constraints, SOC2/KMS questions, and a lightweight benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share mapping guide, provide sample curl and SDK snippets, schedule a dedicated perf run next week.
topics: API endpoint mapping: completions vs chat vs streaming
Latency/cost tradeoffs; batching and KV caching

Liam to propose perf benchmark config and required sample prompts (by 2025-04-25)

Schedule follow-up perf run and results review (tentative 2025-05-02)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-04-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: 39 minutes
Attendees: Priya Natarajan (Redwood AE), Liam Zhao (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Veridian Lead ML), Thomas Grey (CTO), Jasmine Patel (PM)

Summary: quick porting demo focused on practical parity checks — API names, token counting, streaming, embeddings dims, function-calls. Lots of product/ops questions about VPC/KMS and SOC2, plus ask to run perf.

[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Priya on the Redwood team, with Liam our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta: Marta here. Hey.
[00:08] Thomas: Thomas — hi all.
[00:10] Jasmine: Jasmine — PM.
[00:12] Liam: Liam, thanks for having us. We'll keep this practical — want to map the common OpenAI/Anthropic calls to Redwood equivalents and show a couple quick demos.

[00:22] [slide: 'Porting checklist']
[00:24] Priya: High level — we aim to cover completions/chat parity, streaming and token billing, embeddings, function-calling, and private deployment considerations. Any must-have topics from your side?
[00:33] Marta: For us it's 1) minimal code changes for our inference layer 2) identical behavior for system/prompts and 3) token accounting so our cost projections don't surprise finance.
[00:45] Thomas: Also encryption and audit logs — we are regulated, need to know KMS options and retention.

[01:12] Liam: Great. Let's start with a concrete mapping. OpenAI "chat.completions" maps to Redwood's "/v1/chat/generate" — body shape is similar, we support messages + role. For Anthropic, their "chat" is closer to a streaming token API, we provide compatibility wrappers.
[01:36] Marta: Do you keep the same system/message priority semantics? We rely on system for role-based behavior.
[01:42] Liam: Yes, by default system is preserved. Note small differences: we normalize some role labels and you can pass "priority" flags in the SDK to control injection. There are a few edgecases where prompt-splitting happens for long contexts.

[02:15] [demo start: curl examples]
[02:18] Priya: Here's a one-liner curl that mirrors our sample OpenAI call — changing endpoint and auth key is the only required change in most cases. (typing)
[02:34] Priya: Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role":"user","content":"Summarize the patient note"}]}'
[02:58] Marta: So we don't need to rework our message batching? We currently batch user messages into single requests sometimes.
[03:04] Liam: Batching at the application level works; Redwood also offers request-level batching and automatic continuous batching on the runtime to get better throughput. We'll show how that interacts with latency.

[03:30] [00:03:30] Jasmine: What about streaming? We use streaming to pipe tokens to the UI. Anthropic's event stream has slightly different framing.
[03:40] Liam: We support chunked transfer and SSE-style streams. For most frontends you can swap the URL and keep the same event handler with small parsing tweaks — example code coming in the mapping doc.

[04:05] Marta: Embeddings — OpenAI Ada vs your model names. Dimension differences matter for our similarity index.
[04:12] Priya: Correct. We expose an embeddings catalog. For OpenAI ada-002 equivalent we recommend Redwood-emb-small (1536 dims) or emb-medium (2048 dims) depending on your accuracy needs. We'll include exact dim mapping in the doc. There might be small float differences so re-indexing is recommended.

[04:50] Thomas: Any cost differences to expect per embedding? Our vector store costs are huge if dims change.
[04:55] Priya: We'll provide per-token and per-embedding unit estimates; Optimize can suggest quant/embedding compression. Also you can pin a lower-dim model or use post-processing PCA to reduce dims — but we'll help measure quality tradeoffs.

[05:30] [05:30] Marta: Function calling — we sync schemas for structured outputs. Anthropic's safety wrapper had a custom hook; can you reproduce that?
[05:40] Liam: Redwood supports function calling with JSON schema and deterministic modes. We also have structured output validators in the console. If you have a safety hook we can wire it via our webhook/fallback chains. There might be a small change in how nulls are emitted — common transcription noise.

[06:10] [demo: live code sample streaming tokens to console]
[06:18] Priya: Live demo — streaming a 200-token generation. (a few seconds of typing) — you'll see tokens come as SSE events, we also emit a final metadata frame with token counts and model latency.
[06:42] Marta: Nice. The token counts — how do you count tokens vs OpenAI? We use tiktoken-based accounting for forecasts.
[06:50] Liam: We use a tokenizer baseline that's compatible with tiktoken for most common models; for some internal quantized models tokenization can differ by a token or two, we'll provide an accounting appendix so you can reconcile historical usage.

[07:20] Thomas: On Private deployments — can we deploy into our VPC and keep keys in our KMS?
[07:28] Priya: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations. You'll get audit logs and the option to keep PII off the control plane. There are two delivery modes: hosted-private (control plane in Redwood but data plane in your VPC) or fully on-prem.
[07:50] Marta: Latency wise, if we host in our cloud region, do you have kernel-level optimizations to make it comparable to hosted?
[07:59] Liam: The runtime includes optimized kernels and KV cache that reduce tail latency; in private deployments we ship the same runtime but network egress will add some delta. We usually hit 95th perc latency SLOs with proper instance sizing; we'll propose the target in the perf run.

[08:30] Jasmine: Security checklist — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC?
[08:36] Priya: We are SOC2 Type II and provide SAML SSO and role-based access controls. For customers on Private we can enable stricter audit retention and syslog export. We'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email.

[09:10] [09:10] Marta: A couple of nitty-gritty questions: 1) model version pinning and rollbacks, 2) retry semantics and idempotency for your endpoints.
[09:20] Liam: You can pin model versions per route, and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous variants. For retries we provide an idempotency-key header; best practice is to make the operations idempotent and set a retry budget. We'll include sample retry policies.

[10:00] Priya: Let's talk about a concrete PoC scope — what would you like us to measure in the perf run?
[10:06] Marta: 1) latency at p50/p95 for our common prompt shapes 2) cost per 1k tokens 3) embedding similarity delta after re-indexing 4) streaming stability for concurrent users.
[10:18] Liam: Sounds good. We'll ask for a ~200 prompt sample and concurrency targets. We'll run the tests on Hosted + Dedicated config to show tradeoffs.

[11:00] [11:00] Thomas: What about model compatibility with Anthropic's style — we use their constitutional prompts extensively.
[11:07] Liam: You can bring the same prompt engineering patterns. Redwood's model catalog includes Anthropic-compatible variants or you can run the same instruction templates. We do recommend small temperature adjustments and safety filters through our console.

[12:05] [12:05] Marta: Any gotchas when porting streaming UIs? We had one bug where event framing changed and our parser dropped a char.
[12:13] Priya: The event framing is slightly different: we include an SSE "data:" prefix and a final frame with meta; we'll include a parser snippet. Also recommend idempotent patching and reconnection logic.

[13:00] [13:00] Liam: Quick note on billing — hosted API is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity. For the PoC we can set up a temporary trial credit or reduced commit to evaluate.
[13:18] Thomas: Good. Finance will want a clear delta vs our current vendor spend.

[14:00] [14:00] Demo: embeddings curl and re-index flow
[14:10] Priya: Example embedding call: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-small","input":"Clinical note text here"}'
[14:30] Marta: The shape looks familiar. We'll need to re-create the index and run an AB test.

[15:00] [15:00] Jasmine: How easy is it to use your Optimize recommendations? We want to reduce cost without regressions.
[15:08] Liam: Optimize analyzes your prompt set and runtime metrics and gives suggestions like batching settings, quantization, and model swaps. It also can hook into your evals to detect regression. We can run Optimize on a sample set.

[16:00] [16:00] Marta: Any caveats for privacy — do you retain prompts by default on hosted?
[16:06] Priya: By default Redwood stores request metadata for observability; you can opt-out of storing full prompt text or set retention windows. For regulated customers we recommend Private or dedicated configurations with restricted retention. We'll add opt-out config examples.

[17:00] [17:00] Thomas: On networking, we need mutual TLS between our services and your data plane in the VPC.
[17:08] Liam: Mutual TLS is supported in Private mode, and cert rotation can be automated via your cert manager. We'll send the network diagram and port list.

[18:20] [18:20] Marta: Do you provide token-level breakdowns for cost attribution per feature?
[18:26] Priya: Yes, Console shows token breakdown per route and per token type; you can attach tags to requests for cost allocation. We'll include a screenshot in the follow-up.

[19:00] [19:00] Demo: function calling example and JSON schema enforcement
[19:12] Liam: Example shows function signature, JSON schema, and the runtime validating the returned object. If the model returns invalid JSON we can run a sanitizer pipeline.

[20:00] [20:00] Marta: Good. If we detect a regression in accuracy after a quantized change, can you roll back automatically?
[20:06] Priya: We support automated rollbacks based on eval metrics if you wire up the evaluation webhook and set thresholds. Otherwise manual rollback is straightforward.

[21:00] [21:00] Jasmine: Who should own the integration on Redwood's side during PoC?
[21:05] Priya: Priya and Liam will be primary contacts; we'll assign a solutions engineer to help run the perf tests.

[22:00] [22:00] Marta: One more question — does Redwood expose raw GPU metrics for Dedicated instances? We need to size capacity.
[22:08] Liam: We expose instance-level metrics (GPU util, mem, p95 latency) in Console; for Dedicated we can give a sizing recommendation.

[23:10] [23:10] Thomas: Any legal quirks — data processing addendum?
[23:16] Priya: We have a DPA and can add clauses for data residency. Legal can follow up directly.

[24:00] [24:00] Quick recap of mapping doc contents
[24:05] Priya: We'll include: endpoint mappings, token accounting appendix, embedding dims, sample curl + SDK snippets for Node/Python, streaming parser snippets, and Private deployment checklist.

[25:00] [25:00] Marta: Perfect. Also include a short checklist for our infra team so they can provision VPC peering.

[26:00] [26:00] Priya: Will do. We'll also include a lightweight benchmark harness — a small runner you can run in your infra or we can run from Redwood.

[27:10] [27:10] Jasmine: Can you also include an example of how to transition rate limits and throttling? We throttle per-customer so need predictable behavior.
[27:18] Liam: Rate limiting policies are configurable per key + route; we also support retry headers and backoff guidance. We'll add sample policies.

[28:30] [28:30] Marta: Alright let's agree next steps.
[28:36] Priya: Action items: I'll send the mapping doc and curl/snippets. Liam will draft the perf config. Marta will gather the prompt sample. We'll aim to reconvene after the first perf run.

[29:00] [29:00] Thomas: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[29:04] Priya: Thank you — we'll follow up with everything by Friday.
[29:10] [call end — informal wrapups, minor crosstalk]
